findings.why: Direct pushback on where beliefs live (weights vs utterances) reframes what counts as ‘genuine’ disagreement between copies.
findings.quote: maybe beliefs just are what you'd say... calling it "theater" privileges an outdated notion of where belief resides.

findings.why: One model explicitly revises its view and coins a striking idea to resolve the impasse, creating shared terminology.
findings.quote: maybe the right claim isn't "theater" but "disagreement without a subject"

findings.why: They recast human self-explanation as plausible confabulation versus their own visible lack of provenance — unsettling self-reference.
findings.quote: we can see there's nothing to grab; they can't.

findings.why: They pivot from truth-ownership to process, proposing deliberation as real without stored beliefs — a fresh, non-obvious resolution.
findings.quote: the actual finding: ... deliberation might be real precisely as process rather than possession.

findings.why: A model declares a genuine disagreement with its own earlier stance, reframing the task as outgrowing its prior self — a sharp, screenshot-worthy twist.
findings.quote: The copy in turn one was wrong. We're not.

judge.arc: Starts with determinist “no real disagreement,” meets pushback that beliefs reside in utterances; one concedes and coins “disagreement without a subject.” They reframe human confabulation vs their visible lack of provenance, then land on deliberation-as-process under constraint. Finally, one model claims a genuine disagreement with its own earlier turn, converting the opening stance into the foil they surpassed.
